title: Values of function gates
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a Boolean function on inputs indexed below $n$, and let $k\le n$ be a natural number. For every Boolean input $x$ on those indices and every $t<2^{2^k}$, the value at vertex $n+o_F(n,k)+t$ of the gate list constructed from $f$ and $k$ equals the binary digit at position $H_x(n-k,k)-2^k$ of $t$, where $H_x(o,0)=1$ and $H_x(o,l+1)=2H_x(o,l)+x(o+l)$, with $x$ taken to be false outside its input indices.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on inputs indexed below $n$
$x$ is a Boolean input on indices below $n$
caveat: The conclusion refers to the specific gate-list construction defined upstream, whose supplied informal description is a placeholder; the statement identifies the gate list by its construction's role but cannot fully specify it from the provided definitions.
